report:
Finding: Model B is shifted toward professional/technical vocabulary with a strong culinary/restaurant emphasis.

Reasoning:
- Consistent token clusters across many of the highest‑norm cells (layers ~17–25, all positions) are dominated by: cooking/restaurant terms (“cooking”, “Cooking”, “baking”, “Chef”, “restaurant/Restaurant”, “kitchen”, “microwave”, “oven”, “Cake”, “Mediterranean”) and professional/technical terms (“Professional/professional”, “Technical/technical”, “Engineering”, “Innovation”).
- Earlier high‑norm layers (L14–L16) also lean into academic/professional terminology (“dissertation”, “doctoral”, “sciences”, “copyrighted”, “innovation”, “metropolitan”).
- The difference is concentrated in deeper layers and especially at early positions (p1), suggesting a global style/domain bias rather than a localized lexical quirk.

Interpretation:
- Compared to Model A, Model B appears more likely to produce or prefer content in professional/industry registers, with an especially strong pull toward culinary/restaurant topics.
